title: How Celebrities Became America’s Unregulated Drug Pushers
author: Kristen French
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthHow Celebrities Became America’s Unregulated Drug PushersSocial media endorsements can sway consumers, and no one is watchingKFBy Kristen French3:00 PM CDT on July 29, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleA classic Saturday Night Live sketch from more than a decade ago starring Tina Fey features birth-control pills that can turn your baby into a firemonster if you happen to get pregnant, among other deranged risks. The sketch is meant to parody the often bonkers land of TV ads for prescription drugs, where happy people skip through pastel-colored landscapes while a voiceover reports side effects that sometimes sound worse than the condition they aim to treat. Of course, these warnings are required by the FDA, intended to protect credulous and vulnerable consumers against companies that might otherwise present their drugs as cure-alls.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 1058.7K 30Could There Be Another Planet Out In Our Solar System?ShareNextStayBut in recent years, social media has created a massive loophole in the regulation of drug advertising, and celebrities seem to be filling it. Last year, tennis legend Serena Williams starred in a social media campaign launched by telehealth company Ro for GLP-1 drugs she bought on the platform.
